title: Gusteau Recipe
description: One recipe in the Gusteau repository. Genre files (data/*.json) and chef files (data/chefs/*.json) are arrays of these objects.

id.description: Base recipes use a genre prefix (am/mx/it/md/fr/in) plus a number. Chef-attributed recipes use ch-<chef initials>-NNN and must carry a chef object.

genre.description: The four core genres plus two that only chef-attributed recipes use: french (Julia Child, Jacques Pepin) and international (British, fusion and other dishes outside the core four).

subgenre.description: Free-text grouping inside a genre, e.g. burgers, bbq, pasta, pizza, tacos, mezze.

description.description: One sentence shown under the title in browse cards.

difficulty.description: beginner: no technique to learn, hard to ruin. intermediate: multi-component, timing or a technique like searing/emulsifying/dough. advanced: long or fussy — lamination, braise plus sauce, fry temperature control, cured or cooked-to-temp proteins.

easeScore.description: 10 = almost impossible to get wrong; 1 = demanding. Combines active attention, technique, number of steps and timing pressure. Correlates with difficulty: beginner 8-10, intermediate 5-7, advanced 1-4.

spiceScore.description: Capsaicin heat as written. 0 = no heat, 1-2 = warmth only, 3-4 = mild, 5-6 = medium, 7-8 = hot, 9-10 = very hot.

popularity.description: How recognizable and frequently cooked the dish is in the US. 10 = household staple.

pantryScore.description: How likely a typical US home cook already has everything, or can get it at any supermarket in one stop. 10 = pantry and fridge staples only.

cookMin.description: Cooking, baking, resting or marinating time.

equipment.description: The app's Equipment type covers stovetop | oven | microwave; grill and broiler map to oven, air-fryer to oven, slow-cooker and pressure-cooker to stovetop. See README.

ingredients.description: Display strings with amounts, in the order used, e.g. "1 lb ground beef (80/20)".

ingredientKeys.description: Canonical lowercase keys, one per ingredient line, for matching against user inventory.

specialty.description: Subset of ingredientKeys a typical US kitchen will NOT have on hand. Empty array means fully pantry-friendly. Drives the 'missing ingredients' count.

steps.description: Short imperative steps, each one action a beginner can follow without reading ahead.

pescatarian.description: True for vegetarian recipes and for ones whose only animal protein is fish or shellfish.

glutenFree.description: True only if gluten-free as written, assuming certified GF versions of naturally GF staples (oats, soy sauce, broth).

glutenFreeAdaptable.description: True when one swap (GF pasta, GF buns, cornstarch for flour) makes it gluten-free.

nutFree.description: Tree nuts and peanuts. Does not consider cross-contamination.

allergens.description: The US major allergens present as written.

gmo.description: NOT a claim about the dish. A sourcing-risk rating: how likely conventionally-bought ingredients derive from bioengineered crops (corn, soy, canola, sugar beet, cottonseed, some papaya and squash) or from animals raised on them. Buying organic or Non-GMO Project verified lowers every rating to 'low'.

risk.description: low: whole foods, no commodity-crop derivatives. moderate: seed oils, conventional meat or dairy from grain-fed animals, or refined sugar. high: multiple processed or corn/soy-derived components (tortillas, buns, sauces, breading, syrups).

sources.description: Which ingredient families drive the rating.

nutrition.description: Estimated per serving. See README for method and accuracy.

tags.description: Free-form browse facets: quick, one-pan, kid-friendly, meal-prep, high-protein, low-carb, comfort, party, weeknight, date-night, grill, make-ahead, budget, leftovers.

file.description: Filename inside images/. Recipes that are variants of one dish intentionally share a file.

wikipedia.description: English Wikipedia page title whose lead image represents the dish. scripts/fetch_images.py resolves it to a medium-resolution JPEG plus attribution.

chef.description: Present when this recipe is a dish the named chef is known for. The instructions are Gusteau's own - this is an attribution of the dish, not a reproduction of the chef's published recipe text. Absent or null on base recipes.
